text: Cattle have small lungs relative to the animal's overall size, and the lungs sit deep in the chest. The respiratory tract's parts are: muzzle and nostrils, larynx, windpipe, and lungs. The larynx, at the back of the mouth, opens into the trachea, which passes down into the chest where it divides into two bronchi; the bronchi branch into smaller bronchi. The respiratory tract is lined by a mucous membrane, so called because it is bathed in sticky mucus.
